title: Weekly POC Velocity & Contrast - Odyssey Therapeutics
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest micro-benchmark results: p50/p95 latency and throughput vs current baseline vendor. Redwood showed improved cost per token with slight p95 regression at 1024 tokens; tuning items: aggressive batching limits, prefix KV cache warmup, quantization profile change, and routing thresholds. Next steps agreed: run 1-hour head-to-head on customer's production-like workload, deliver updated benchmark spreadsheet, schedule dedicated-slot trial, and share security/KMS doc link.
topics: quantization profile impact on quality and speed

Priya Nair: Configure dedicated trial slot template and post run playbook by 2025-03-10

next_steps: Run 1-hour head-to-head load test w/ customer's 30-min production sample (Marcus + Aisha) - target week of 2025-03-10

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-05 15:00 PST | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Marcus Li (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (CTO, Odyssey), Marisol Vega (SRE), Aisha Khan (ML Eng)

[00:00] Marcus: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, uh quick check we got 45 minutes on the calendar, is that still good?
[00:05] Ethan: yep, that works for us, we've got time to walk through the numbers.
[00:12] Marcus: cool. quick agenda: run through the microbench numbers vs your baseline, point out where we saw gaps, then tuning options and next steps. Priya will run the deeper perf bits.
[00:22] Priya: alright I'll share my screen in a sec, but main takeaway up front, p50 is generally lower for us across short sequences, p95 is where the incumbent is a touch better at longer sequences around 1k tokens on your prompt shapes. throughput at steady-state was better for Redwood when batching is enabled.
[00:40] Aisha: can you quantify that? like what are we seeing at 512 and 1024?
[00:45] Priya: sure, so microbench -- p50 at 512 tokens: Redwood 78ms vs IncumbentVendorX 120ms, p95 512: Redwood 210ms vs 230ms. At 1024 tokens p50 Redwood 170ms vs 220ms, p95 Redwood 520ms vs 480ms (so incumbent edges us at p95 there).
[01:10] Marisol: that p95 at 1024 is the thing that worries us; those are our worst-case latency SLOs.
[01:15] Marcus: totally, we expected that tradeoff. a few hypotheses: KV cache warmup on your specific traffic, the incumbent might be using a slightly different kernel path / longer context optimizations, and our quant profile default was safer for quality, which costs cycles.
[01:30] Ethan: interesting. so does that mean we can tune it to close that p95 gap without +50% cost?
[01:35] Priya: yes, usually. We tested three tuning levers this week: increase batching up to 32, enable prefix K-V cache pre-warm, and try int8 quant with per-channel dequant where possible. The int8 run shaved 20% CPU/GPU time but added small quality diffs on some entity-heavy prompts.
[02:00] Aisha: yeah we saw hallucination spikes on a couple examples with int8, not acceptable for the clinical summaries.
[02:06] Priya: understood, so we ran a mixed strategy: keep int8 for shorter contexts and fallback to int16/FP16 for >800 tokens. That reduced p95 by about 12% on mixed traffic without the quality regression on long docs.
[02:25] Marcus: throughput story: under steady QPS 250 we saw Redwood sustain 3.6k tokens/s on 2xA100-equivalent while baseline was 2.9k tokens/s. but if you force worst-case single-shot 1k requests concurrently, our p95 climbs.
[02:45] Marisol: what's the memory/kv implications of that mixed-quant approach? does that blow up memory so we can't run more concurrent slots?
[02:52] Priya: good question. the mixed profile increases peak memory by ~8% because we keep per-request fp16 buffers for long-context fallbacks. but we can mitigate with smarter routing and early detection of long-context requests in the front proxy so we route those to nodes pre-configured for high-memory runs.
[03:15] Ethan: ok routing sounds doable. can Redwood match our VPC requirements for the dedicated slot?
[03:20] Marcus: yes; for the pilot we offer a private dedicated slot inside your VPC with KMS integration. Marisol, we'll share the KMS notes after this call.
[03:28] Marisol: please do, we need HSM/KMS docs for audit. also log retention and slow-trace export procedure from your console.
[03:35] Priya: noted, I'll attach the audit log export steps.
[03:40] Ethan: on the bench set: what exactly did you run? i.e., traffic mix, token distributions?
[03:45] Priya: short version: we replayed your 30-min anonymized sample you gave last week with a synthetic burst pattern (95th percentile bursts at 4x baseline). We did runs at concurrency 16/32 and tuned batch windows. Key metrics are in the CSV I uploaded to the shared folder.
[04:05] Marcus: quick caveat on the transcript import - sometimes the tokenization differs vs your e2e prod tokenizer, which can shift the token counts ~5-8% and effect p50 numbers. so for final head-to-head we need your exact tokenizer so token counts match.
[04:25] Aisha: yep will share our tokenizer config and a 30-min sample by tomorrow.
[04:28] Priya: perfect. another note: we saw a steady-state throughput advantage because of our continuous batching implementation; but at small tail bursts the incumbent's tuned kernel path was slightly faster for that 1k tail. We have a couple options: 1) raise batching aggressiveness but keep a hard latency cap, 2) reserve a small pool of low-latency nodes (dedicated hot path) for long-context requests, or 3) accept slightly higher p95 but lower cost.
[05:00] Ethan: option 2 sounds reasonable if cost is contained. how much extra would that be?
[05:05] Marcus: rough math: a hot-path pool of 2 GPUs during peak window increases pilot cost ~12% but knocks the p95 at 1k tokens below incumbent numbers in our tests. We'll put exact numbers in the benchmark sheet.
[05:18] Marisol: we also need to understand failure modes and fallback. if the hot pool is saturated what's your fallback?
[05:23] Priya: fallback is automated routing to a compatible variant (quantized or smaller model) with an explicit degrade message or we can fail open to incumbent (if you enable that policy). We can instrument a soft-fail that returns a partial response plus a hint for re-try.
[05:40] Aisha: would prefer degrade-with-safety, not failing to vendor in the middle of a sensitive workflow.
[05:45] Marcus: absolutely, we can set policies to never route externally for pilot.
[05:48] Ethan: what about synthetic burst tests? can we run a 1-hour head-to-head identical replay?
[05:52] Marcus: yes, that's our proposed next step. we'll provision a dedicated 2-GPU slot in your VPC for the run. Priya will run the test and upload raw traces.
[06:03] Priya: regarding traces, keep an eye on the KV cache hit rate. we saw warmup issues in first 30s that pushed p95 up; warm caches cut p95 dramatically. Suggest we run a cache-warm phase before measuring.
[06:20] Marisol: good point - we can prime the cache with a 5-minute ramp.
[06:24] Priya: ok. one more item: quality checks. since you flagged hallucination on int8 earlier, we'll include a small suite of eval prompts to validate quality is within your thresholds during the head-to-head.
[06:36] Aisha: great. can we also instrument token-level cost breakdown per request? we need to compare unit economics.
[06:40] Marcus: yes - console will show per-request token cost, and we'll export a CSV with cost and latency columns.
[06:47] Ethan: what about SLA language for the pilot? do we get any uptime/latency commitments?
[06:51] Marcus: for pilot we provide best-effort; dedicated reserved capacity carries SLA. We'll outline a pilot-level commitment in the email (response time for support is standard). If pilot shows fit we can move to reserved and discuss SLA terms.
[07:04] Marisol: timeline check - when can we run the head-to-head?
[07:07] Marcus: if you share payloads/tokenizer by 2025-03-06, we can schedule the 1-hour test on 2025-03-11. Priya can do the run and upload traces same day.
[07:15] Aisha: that works for our team.
[07:18] Marcus: ok wrapping with recap.
[07:20] Marcus: recap: Redwood to send detailed benchmark CSV + raw traces, provision 2-GPU dedicated pilot slot in Odyssey VPC, run 1-hour head-to-head with 5-minute warmup on 2025-03-11, include quality eval suite, and provide KMS/HSM + audit logging doc.
[07:36] Ethan: sounds good. thanks all.
[07:39] Marisol: thanks.
[07:40] Marcus: thanks team, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invite.
[07:45] (call ends)

Notes/Imperfect transcriptions observed: occasionally "K V cash" instead of KV cache, "incumbent vendor" transcribed as "ink-come vendor" in auto notes. CROSSTALK at times; speaker attribution sometimes generic.
